The primary endpoint, named Survival and Recovery Trajectory, will be a composite of 90-day all-cause mortality and, among survivors, a daily ordinal scale analyzed as a trajectory of illness and recovery to 28 days.

text_40: Mortality is defined as death from any cause before the end of study day 90.
The trajectory of patients will be modelled through a Markov longitudinal proportional odds model, using daily ordinal scale categories.

The estimand is the transition between categories and the relative time spent in each category, modelled to produce an odds ratio from an ordinal logistic model, incorporating covariate adjustment as described in Section 7.8.3.

We acknowledge mortality is tied to a longer time frame than the ordinal scale, however integrating 90-day mortality with a shorter-term outcome is patient-centered, allows continuity with previous versions of the Core protocol and the Pandemic Appendix to Core, and improves statistical power.
90-day mortality will be hierarchically integrated with the daily ordinal scale so that 90-day mortality will be deemed the worst possible category, regardless of prior trajectory.

Two additional exploratory outcome measures will be reported.
Survival and Recovery Trajectory Survival and Recovery Trajectory is a composite of all-cause mortality at day 90 and, among survivors, a daily ordinal scale of illness and recovery to 28 days.

The trajectory will be analyzed with a statistical model (Markov longitudinal proportional odds model) that captures how patients move through different health states over time, reported as an odds ratio with covariate adjustment.

The Respiratory Infection Ordinal Weighted Score will use the same ordinal scale categories as in the Survival and Recovery Trajectory described above but will be transformed to a numeric value between 0 (best) and 1 (worst) that reflects the severity of a patient’s illness and recovery trajectory over 28 days.
All patients who die on or before day 90 will be assigned a score of ‘1’.

For patients who survive to day 90, each day's ordinal status is converted to its corresponding mortality-derived weight, and the score is calculated as the mean of these daily weights over the first 28 days.
This will create a score reflecting whether and how quickly they recovered, where better health states receive weights closer to 0.
The weights for each daily ordinal status will be derived from existing REMAP-CAP data and correspond to the estimated probability of 90-day mortality for that category.
The ordinal weighted score will be analyzed with a covariate-adjusted linear model, and effects will be reported as a difference in average scores between treatment groups.
As exploratory outcomes, the exact categorizations of respiratory support may change in both of the above exploratory outcomes, which will be transparently reported in publications and presentations.
